title: docs: add capacity, scope and lifecycle rules to model policy
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Lessons from the first Azure catalog run (#15304, #15306, #15317, #15320), written into the model-management policy so the next models don't repeat them.

- Capacity: unused Azure Global Standard capacity costs nothing, so size token limits to the largest accepted request. GPT-5.3 Codex at 10K TPM rejects any ~15K-token prompt with a 429 at zero traffic. Scarce image pools are sized from measured demand instead.
- Scope: add models that are differentiated; close superseded versions of an already-public family instead of queuing them.
- Lifecycle: migrate public models facing retirement before new additions, keep the two-month cutoff for new models, and treat Preview routes as short-lived.
- Economics: credits are used by traffic volume, not catalog breadth, so moving high-volume cash-spend traffic onto credit-eligible routes comes first.
- Latency: non-streaming text beyond about 125s is unreliable on the gateway (GPT-5.4 Pro took 314s at default effort), so reasoning-heavy routes need a non-streaming latency check.
- Test matrix: adds the max-size request and non-streaming latency checks.

gist.headline: A field guide for models
gist.blurb: The first Azure catalog run left useful notes in the margins. They’re now part of the model-management policy, with checks for prompts that don’t fit and responses that take their time.
gist.summary: Documented Azure model-management rules for capacity, catalog scope, and lifecycle, and added max-size request and non-streaming latency checks after a 10K TPM route rejected a roughly 15K-token prompt and a reasoning-heavy route exceeded the gateway’s roughly 125-second reliable window.
gist.impact: Model operators now have concrete checks for accepted prompt size and non-streaming latency, plus guidance to prioritize retirement migrations and differentiated additions.
gist.visual_concept: An internal model-management field guide sits beside a retro terminal: a stack of token blocks tests whether a route can hold a full prompt, while a small clock marks the latency check. Polli, wearing tiny reading glasses, annotates the guide; code-plants and a lime-green desk lamp keep the scene warm.
